sentences.text: Kank was a medium-sized unenlagiid dinosaur, a type of theropod, with bones roughly the size of those found in Neuquenraptor. Scientists estimate that Neuquenraptor weighed about 27 kg, giving Kank a similar mass.

This animal possessed small, apically curved teeth that lacked serrations. The upper jaw teeth were straight without lingual curvature and compressed from side to side in cross-section. These teeth featured apicobasally oriented flutes around lateral grooves but no serrated ridges. In contrast, the lower jaw teeth had mesial ridges restricted to the top third of the crown, a trait similar to Austroraptor.
The genus Kank is currently considered a valid taxon discovered in the Chorrillo Formation in southwestern Patagonia, Argentina. The type locality for this species is the Chorrillo Formation.

The holotype of Kank is a single vertebra designated as specimen MPM-PV-23106-A. Three toe bones and five teeth were found alongside the holotype vertebra. Kank was described by Motta and colleagues, a team authored by Matías J. Motta, Alexis M. Aranciaga Rolando, and eleven other researchers.

The genus name Kank honors the "elder Rhea" from Aonikenk mythology, who created the Southern Cross constellation. The species name australis means "from the south" in Latin, referring to the discovery location.
Fossils associated with Kank include fish remains, suggesting it lived in a wetland environment containing both terrestrial and freshwater areas.
Kank is classified as a member of the unenlagiid theropod group. The parent group of Kank is the family Unenlagiidae. Kank belongs to the class Reptilia.
Kank lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age. This corresponds to a time between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
